children: climbs 2.8% in Wednesday's trading as J.P. Morgan upgraded the oil giant to Overweight from Neutral and hiked its price target to 675 pence (~$54) from 550 pence, after the stock has lagged its closest rivals over the last 3-5 years.
JPM analysts led by Matthew Lofting said a combination of supportive macro conditions and internal renewal now offered a major opportunity to reduce BP's
sensitivity to the oil price cycle and strengthen its fundamentals into 2028.

balance sheet improvement means the stock is "no longer a poison pill," Lofting and his team said, estimating that by year-end 2027, the company's total financial obligations will have declined by 50%, to take gearing metrics back in line with European peers for the first time in the current decade.

"This drives significant improvement in the ratio of financial expenses/dividends, signaling potential for a debt-to-equity value transfer which sees BP return to distribution growth," the analysts wrote.
JPM also sees value in BP's
restructuring drive, which the bank believes is worth the equivalent of a high-single-digit percentage annual growth in underlying earnings per share over three years.
to Neutral from Overweight, noting the company's highest direct asset exposure to the Middle East among European companies, as well as the possibility of windfall taxes.
